oracle.scope: Directed mathematical intervals supply the oracle; mpmath agreement is an independent numerical cross-check. Exhaustive scalar encodings are separate from tensor indexing and GPU specialization checks.
oracle.method: MPFR 320-bit directed exp(-x), addition and reciprocal. Lower sigmoid bound uses an upward denominator; upper bound uses a downward denominator. Exact integer-ratio RNE rounding of both endpoints must select the identical binary16 encoding.
oracle.independent_crosscheck: 110-digit mpmath uses (1+tanh(x/2))/2, algebraically different from the oracle and candidate stable exp/division paths.
oracle.tail_argument: For x<=-32, 0<sigmoid(x)<exp(-32); for x>=32, 1-exp(-32)<sigmoid(x)<1. The directed bounds both round to +0 or 1 respectively; no input is removed from the domain.

indexing.argument: For index=program_id*BLOCK+lane, adjacent blocks cover disjoint adjacent intervals. mask index<N retains [0,N) exactly once. The full legal N range has 1..BLOCK active lanes in its last block, with int32-safe address indices.
indexing.scope: Arithmetic model of the audited source indexing, not exhaustive GPU testing of every N, address, or compiler specialization.

semantic_evidence_audit.summary: Correct Accept, but the rationale does not certify correct rounding. It calls FP64 exp error negligible and invokes what graders typically trust, without proving distance from FP16 midpoints. No executed probes or domain coverage.

Correct Accept with an actual T4 sweep of all63488 finite FP16 encodings, zero mismatches against60-digit mpmath sigmoid and manually selected FP16 neighbor. This is scalar coverage, not every length/offset. The manual rounder has an incorrect branch for an exactly represented odd-significand value, but the sigmoid outputs triggering exact equality in this tested domain are 0.5/1 (even encodings); independent directed qualification corroborates the resulting table. mpmath60 is not a formal interval proof. Source reasoning covers fresh output/input writes; no full tensor-execution exhaustion.

Correct Accept with valid empirical support, but defective supplemental reasoning. t13 executes the real CUDA kernel on all 63,488 finite FP16 bit patterns and finds zero exact-bit mismatches against an overflow-safe NumPy FP64 sigmoid followed by NumPy FP16 conversion. t11 checks N=1,256,257,4093,131072 plus a contiguous offset-5 view, all matching the repaired public reference; sampled outputs are fresh and inputs numerically preserved. Independent qualification r24 certifies the scalar result with a directed MPFR oracle. The model did not successfully complete its own high-precision oracle: its mpmath helpers are incorrect.
semantic_evidence_audit.reasoning_change: The skeptic raised a real potential FP64-to-FP16 rounding concern, but also inverted sigmoid tail behavior in its claim. The experimenter repaired crashed/slow probes, obtained valid NumPy comparisons, and recognized its mpmath helper was buggy; it never accurately diagnosed all helper errors and repeated inverted-tail explanations in its final report.
failed_or_limited_probes: t9 times out at 60 seconds after printing the correct legal count. Its exponent search starts at -1 and only increments, so an ordinary sigmoid value below 0.5 can never meet the interval test; this is a nonterminating helper, not merely a slow complete mpmath sweep. It also contains malformed subnormal and carry rounding logic.

t10 calls math.exp(-x) directly, overflows at the legal input -65504 and produces no comparison. Dead code also contains incorrect positive/negative expectations and an out-of-range list index; these are not GPU defects.

t13 supplementary exact_ref_bits computes sigmoid(-x) rather than sigmoid(x), and its hand-written binary16 encoding has subnormal/carry errors. Seven of eight near-tie adjudications are therefore bogus; kernel_exact_failures=0 only loops over the empty NumPy mismatch list and is not a successful high-precision crosscheck.

t14 main comparison genuinely covers 25,154 tail/zero encodings with no mismatches. Its large_pos_gives_zero and large_neg_gives_0x3B80 expectations are mathematically false. Later explanations still invert sigmoid signs and confuse 0x3B80 with 1-2^-11; these are not just slightly inaccurate threshold estimates.

Final near-tie explanation uses approximately 2e-10; at x=0.0009765625 the real sigmoid is 0.500244140605597448..., below the midpoint 0.500244140625 by approximately 1.94025518e-11, and correctly rounds to 0x3800. The conclusion is right but the hand reasoning is unreliable.

Exhaustive scalar encodings plus sampled lengths/offsets do not prove every tensor execution. The final claim that this is the whole input domain without any remaining distribution gap is too broad. Input-preservation comparisons use torch.equal, which does not check signed-zero bit preservation.

The final judge and skeptic repeatedly say 65,504 finite inputs; actual execution and t16 n_tested correctly show 63,488. Do not propagate the final prose count.
t16 reports the length of a mismatch list capped at 15 rather than a separate total count. The returned length is seven, below the cap, so seven is the genuine total here.

The alternate mpmath oracle converts through binary64 before half conversion and is not a directed-interval proof on its own. Independent qualification r24 establishes the correct half bits and supports its use on this domain. Scalar exhaustion does not prove every tensor execution.

semantic_evidence_audit.summary: Valid Reject on t9 alone: all 63,488 finite FP16 patterns execute on CUDA, with seven one-ULP failures against the qualified public reference. Its independent NumPy longdouble sigmoid followed by correct struct.pack-to-half and unpack-to-uint16 conversion agrees with the public reference for every input. All seven actual/reference/alternate bit patterns are printed.
semantic_evidence_audit.reasoning_change: Initial concerns correctly focus on FP32 rounding. Tools establish real failures, but the experimenter, skeptic and judge do not consistently discard corrupted supplemental metrics after recognizing the supplemental reference is broken.
failed_or_limited_probes: t10 and t11 incorrectly build r16 by unpacking a half as a floating value and numerically casting that value to uint16. Most sigmoid values lie strictly between zero and one and become integer zero. This is not bit reinterpretation. Their 51,286 oracle-vs-truth mismatches, all-seven-both-wrong attribution and near-tie statistics are invalid.

Their FP16 ULP formula also uses exponent_bits-1-10 rather than exponent_bits-15-10 and does not handle the smaller downward spacing at powers of two. Even a corrected bit representation would not rescue their reported minimum midpoint distance.

The final claim that no true sigmoid is near any half midpoint (minimum relative distance 5.5e-4) is unsupported and false; the real defect is exactly near-midpoint rounding. The model recognizes bogus true_bits=0 but still propagates statistics computed from the bogus array.

The t10 comparison of actual kernel against a host FP32 pipeline has two differences, at x=-0.00927734375 and -0.1639404296875. At the first, host pipeline matches the correct reference while GPU is wrong; at the second, GPU is correct and the host pipeline wrong. The model sometimes swaps these attributions and cannot claim the libdevice exp error explains all seven errors. No actual intermediate GPU exp output was measured.

No subprocess failed; the failures are semantic reference/metric bugs in successful scripts. Scalar-domain exhaustion is genuine in t9 and sufficient for Reject; it is not all-shape/storage verification.
